candidates.original_title: What is going on around here? Intolerance of uncertainty predicts threat generalization
candidates.description: Higher intolerance of uncertainty is associated with greater threat generalization during acquisition training and delayed learning of cue pairings during extinction training
candidates.citation_sentence: Here, we attempted a three-lab direct and conceptual replication of Morriss and colleagues' (2016a) original results.
candidates.notes: Conceptual replication 2 at Texas A&M University used the same general paradigm with ERP measures and modified timing; SCR and LPP findings partially aligned with the original (higher IU showed greater threat generalization and increased threat differentiation during extinction) but ratings did not show the expected phase X IU interaction.
